images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A small wall cabinet about the size of a microwave hangs at the back of a pale neutral tabletop, its body brushed graphite, its door a pane of sandblasted frosted glass in a slim graphite frame. Behind the glass a round glass coffee pot sits full on a warming plate, a faint haze of steam against the frosted pane. The one acid-lime element is the small padlock on the door hasp, shut tight. In front of the cabinet, a single empty frosted glass mug waits on the tabletop, a brown ring dried inside it, and a graphite spoon lies beside it on a folded ivory napkin. Fine dust sits on the hasp, and faint smudges dull the graphite handle. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A wide dry basin stretches to a hazy ridge on the horizon, its floor a cracked crust of pale ivory silt scattered with mug shards like frosted gravel, broken handles poking up in rows where the queues once stood. At the basin's edge stands the cabinet, now the size of a house, its graphite body pitted and its frosted door smashed open, the old padlock dulled to grey. Inside, the pot sits dry and cracked on its plate. A slim graphite pipe stand has been run across the basin from the far ridge on thin legs, and at its end an acid-lime tap valve is turned open, a thin clear stream of coffee just beginning to fall into the empty pot. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface.
